description: The JPEG adversarial attack crafts perturbations that remain effective even after JPEG compression, making adversarial examples robust to common image preprocessing. It leverages gradient-based optimization to generate perturbations that survive lossy compression.
mechanism: 1. Compute gradients of the model loss with respect to the input image. 2. Optimize perturbations in the pixel or frequency domain to maximize misclassification while constraining changes to survive JPEG compression. 3. Apply the perturbation to the image. 4. Optionally, simulate JPEG compression during optimization to ensure robustness.
defence_mechanism: A-JPEG applies adaptive JPEG compression as a preprocessing step to remove adversarial perturbations, while PAT (Pixel Adaptive Transformation) adaptively transforms pixels to disrupt structured adversarial noise, both aiming to destroy perturbations that survive standard JPEG.
variants: JPEG-resistant adversarial examples, Compression-aware adversarial attacks, None well-known
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires access to model gradients and knowledge of JPEG compression parameters
target_vulnerability: Exploits the model's sensitivity to small, structured perturbations that persist through common image preprocessing like JPEG compression

description: StAdv is an adversarial attack that generates visible perturbations by spatially transforming input images to fool CNN classifiers. Instead of adding pixel-wise noise, it warps the image geometry to induce misclassification.
mechanism: 1. Compute the gradient of the loss with respect to a spatial transformation field (e.g., flow field) rather than pixel values. 2. Optimize the transformation field to maximize the model's prediction error while constraining the spatial distortion to remain perceptually plausible. 3. Apply the optimized spatial transformation to the input image to generate the adversarial example.
defence_mechanism: A-StAdv and PAT (Pixel-wise Adversarial Training) defend by augmenting training data with spatially transformed adversarial examples, enabling the model to learn invariance to such geometric perturbations and reducing susceptibility to StAdv attacks.
variants: Spatially Transformed Adversarial Examples (stAdv), Adversarial Spatial Transformations, None well-known
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to the model architecture and gradients
target_vulnerability: Exploits the model's sensitivity to small spatial deformations and lack of robustness to geometric transformations

description: ReColorAdv is an adversarial attack that generates visible color-based perturbations to fool convolutional neural networks (CNNs) by altering the color distribution of input images.
mechanism: 1. The attacker learns a color transformation matrix that, when applied to an image, shifts its color channels. 2. This transformation is optimized to maximize the model's prediction error while keeping the image visually plausible. 3. The perturbed image is then fed to the CNN, causing misclassification.
defence_mechanism: A-ReCAdv and PAT (Pixel-wise Adversarial Training) defend by augmenting training data with recolor adversarial examples, improving model robustness to color-based perturbations.
variants: ColorFool, AdvCF, None well-known
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires access to model parameters and gradients to optimize the color transformation
target_vulnerability: CNNs' sensitivity to color distribution and reliance on color cues for classification

description: Label Propagation Attack (LPA) is a data poisoning attack where adversarially crafted samples are injected into the training set to manipulate the learned decision boundaries of a CNN, often by exploiting label propagation algorithms.
mechanism: 1. The attacker generates poisoned samples with carefully chosen features and incorrect labels. 2. These samples are injected into the training data. 3. During training, the CNN's decision boundaries are influenced by the poisoned data, causing misclassification. 4. The attack leverages the label propagation process to amplify the effect of the poisoned samples.
defence_mechanism: A-LPA (Adversarial Label Propagation Algorithm) and PAT (Poisoning-Aware Training) detect and mitigate the influence of poisoned samples by identifying anomalous label propagation patterns and reweighting or filtering suspicious data during training.
variants: None well-known
threat_model: grey-box; attacker can inject or modify a subset of training data but may not have full knowledge of the model parameters
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to training data manipulation and the reliance of label propagation algorithms on local data structure

description: Fast-LPA is a label poisoning attack that injects mislabeled samples into the training data to degrade the performance of CNN models. The attack aims to maximize the impact of poisoned labels while minimizing the number of poisoned samples.
mechanism: 1. Select a subset of training samples to poison based on their influence on the model's loss. 2. Flip the labels of these selected samples to incorrect classes. 3. Inject the mislabeled samples into the training set. 4. Retrain the CNN model on the poisoned dataset, causing it to learn incorrect mappings.
defence_mechanism: A-Fast-LPA detects and removes suspiciously mislabeled samples using anomaly detection, while PAT (Pattern-Attribution Training) increases model robustness by regularizing attributions to reduce sensitivity to poisoned labels.
variants: A-Fast-LPA, Clean-Label Attacks, Backdoor Label Flipping
threat_model: white-box; attacker has access to the training data and can modify labels
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to label noise and their tendency to overfit to mislabeled data

description: FGSM (Fast Gradient Sign Method) generates adversarial examples by adding a small, optimal perturbation to input images in the direction of the gradient of the loss with respect to the input, causing CNNs to misclassify them.
mechanism: 1. Compute the gradient of the loss with respect to the input image. 2. Take the sign of the gradient to determine the direction of perturbation. 3. Multiply by a small epsilon value to control perturbation magnitude. 4. Add this perturbation to the original input to create the adversarial example.
defence_mechanism: M-FGSM (Momentum Iterative FGSM) and Mustafa's methods defend by incorporating momentum into the gradient updates, making adversarial training more robust and reducing the effectiveness of single-step attacks like FGSM by smoothing the loss landscape and improving generalization to adversarial examples.
variants: I-FGSM, M-FGSM, PGD, BIM
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to the model architecture and gradients
target_vulnerability: The attack exploits the model's linearity and high sensitivity to small, input-aligned perturbations in high-dimensional space.

description: The Basic Iterative Method (BIM) generates adversarial examples by iteratively applying small, optimal perturbations to input images, causing CNNs to misclassify them.
mechanism: 1. Compute the gradient of the loss with respect to the input image. 2. Apply a small step in the direction of the sign of the gradient (as in FGSM). 3. Clip the perturbed image to ensure it stays within an epsilon-ball of the original. 4. Repeat steps 1-3 for several iterations to accumulate the perturbation.
defence_mechanism: M-BIM (Mustafa's BIM) introduces randomness or modifies the iterative process (e.g., by varying step sizes or directions) to make the attack less effective, and may include adversarial training with BIM-generated examples to improve robustness.
variants: I-FGSM, PGD, Momentum Iterative Method (MIM), None well-known
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to model architecture and gradients
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to small, adversarially crafted perturbations due to high-dimensional, non-linear decision boundaries

description: Projected Gradient Descent (PGD) is an iterative adversarial attack that perturbs input images to maximize model prediction error while keeping changes within a specified norm bound.
mechanism: 1. Compute the gradient of the loss with respect to the input image. 2. Iteratively update the input by taking small steps in the direction of the gradient, projecting back into the allowed perturbation set after each step. 3. Repeat for a fixed number of iterations or until convergence. 4. Output the final perturbed image as the adversarial example.
defence_mechanism: M-PGD and BAT (Bilateral Adversarial Training) defend by incorporating adversarial examples, often generated via multi-step PGD, into the training process, making the model robust to similar iterative attacks.
variants: FGSM, BIM, CW, DeepFool, AutoAttack
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to model parameters and gradients
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to small, norm-bounded input perturbations due to high-dimensional, non-linear decision boundaries

description: FrogsAttack generates visible adversarial examples for CNNs by applying gradient-based perturbations that resemble frog-like patterns, aiming to mislead the model while being perceptible to humans.
mechanism: 1. Compute the gradient of the loss with respect to the input image using the target CNN. 2. Apply a structured perturbation constrained to frog-like visual patterns, guided by the gradient direction. 3. Iteratively adjust the perturbation to maximize misclassification while maintaining the visible pattern. 4. Output the adversarial image with the embedded frog pattern.
defence_mechanism: A-FrogsAttacks/Data Sanitizing detects and removes or corrects inputs containing characteristic frog-like perturbations by filtering or preprocessing, thereby neutralizing the adversarial effect before inference.
variants: None well-known
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to the model architecture and gradients
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to gradient-based adversarial perturbations, especially when structured in visually salient patterns

description: CollisionAttack is a data poisoning attack where adversarial samples are crafted to collide in feature space with legitimate samples, causing misclassification during inference.
mechanism: 1. The attacker injects poisoned samples into the training data that are visually similar to benign samples but have manipulated labels. 2. These poisoned samples are optimized to have feature representations (e.g., CNN embeddings) that collide with those of target legitimate samples. 3. During training, the model learns to associate the target's features with the incorrect label, leading to targeted misclassification.
defence_mechanism: A-Collision Attack/Data Sanitizing detects and removes training samples that cause abnormal feature space collisions or have suspiciously high similarity to other samples, thereby preventing poisoned samples from influencing the model.
variants: Feature Collision Attack, Clean-Label Poisoning, None well-known
threat_model: white-box or grey-box; attacker needs access to the training data and knowledge of the model's feature extractor
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of deep models to memorizing poisoned samples that collide in feature space with legitimate data

description: The One Shot Kill attack introduces a single, highly effective adversarial example that causes a CNN to misclassify with high confidence. This attack is visible, meaning the perturbation is perceptible to humans.
mechanism: 1. The attacker crafts a single input image with a large, visible perturbation. 2. This image is specifically designed to exploit the CNN's learned features, causing a targeted or untargeted misclassification. 3. The attack does not rely on iterative or gradient-based search; the perturbation is applied in one step. 4. The adversarial example is then presented to the model, resulting in immediate misclassification.
defence_mechanism: A-One Shot-kill/ DS defence detects and rejects inputs with large, visible perturbations by measuring input deviation from the training distribution or using statistical anomaly detection, thereby blocking the attack.
variants: None well-known
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to the model architecture and parameters to craft the adversarial example
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to large, out-of-distribution perturbations that exploit their over-reliance on specific learned features

description: APGD (Auto-PGD) is an iterative adversarial attack that automatically tunes its step size to find minimal perturbations that fool a neural network, typically under an Lp norm constraint.
mechanism: 1. Initialize the input with a small random perturbation within the allowed norm ball. 2. Iteratively update the perturbation using projected gradient descent, adaptively adjusting the step size based on the loss landscape. 3. After each step, project the perturbed input back onto the allowed norm ball. 4. Repeat until convergence or a maximum number of iterations is reached.
defence_mechanism: A-APGD uses adversarial training with APGD-generated examples to increase robustness, while Pixel Defend preprocesses inputs to remove adversarial perturbations by projecting them onto the manifold of natural images.
variants: APGD-CE, APGD-DLR, APGD-T, None well-known
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to model parameters and gradients
target_vulnerability: Exploits the model's sensitivity to small, carefully crafted input perturbations that maximize loss

description: Score-based attacks generate adversarial examples by iteratively modifying input images and using the model's output scores to guide perturbations, aiming to mislead CNN classifiers.
mechanism: 1. The attacker queries the CNN with perturbed versions of the input and observes the output scores (e.g., softmax probabilities). 2. Using either salient search (targeting high-impact pixels) or random perturbations, the attacker updates the input to maximize the target class score or minimize the true class score. 3. This process repeats until the input is misclassified or a perturbation budget is reached.
defence_mechanism: A-SB/Stochastic Element introduces randomness into the model's prediction process, making score feedback unreliable for guiding attacks, while Sharpened Edges preprocessing reduces the effectiveness of small, localized perturbations by enhancing edge features and suppressing subtle noise.
variants: NES attack, SimBA, Square Attack, Bandits Attack
threat_model: black-box; attacker can query the model and observe output scores but has no access to model internals or gradients
target_vulnerability: The attack exploits the model's output score sensitivity to small input changes and the ability to probe the model repeatedly via queries.

description: JSMA (Jacobian-based Saliency Map Attack) generates adversarial examples by iteratively modifying input features that most influence the model's output, aiming to misclassify the input with minimal changes.
mechanism: 1. Compute the forward derivative (Jacobian) of the model with respect to the input to identify features most affecting the target class. 2. Construct a saliency map highlighting input features whose perturbation increases the target class probability and decreases others. 3. Iteratively perturb the most salient features within a constraint (e.g., pixel value bounds) until misclassification or a perturbation limit is reached.
defence_mechanism: M-JSMA introduces randomness (stochastic element) in feature selection to reduce attack effectiveness, while sharpening edges in input preprocessing diminishes the impact of small, localized perturbations by making subtle changes more detectable or less effective.
variants: M-JSMA, Targeted JSMA, Black-box JSMA
threat_model: White-box; attacker requires full access to model architecture and gradients.
target_vulnerability: Exploits the model's sensitivity to small, targeted input perturbations due to high input dimensionality and local linearity in CNNs.

description: The Carlini & Wagner (C&W) attack generates minimal, often imperceptible, perturbations to input images that cause a CNN to misclassify them.
mechanism: 1. Formulate an optimization problem that minimizes the perturbation norm while ensuring misclassification. 2. Use a differentiable surrogate loss (e.g., hinge loss) to penalize correct classification. 3. Apply gradient-based optimization (e.g., Adam) to iteratively update the input until the adversarial objective is met.
defence_mechanism: M-C&W introduces randomness or modifies the C&W loss to make optimization harder; stochastic elements (e.g., randomization layers) disrupt gradient-based attacks; sharpened edges preprocessing removes subtle perturbations by enhancing image edges, reducing attack effectiveness.
variants: L2 C&W, L0 C&W, L∞ C&W, Elastic-Net Attack (EAD)
threat_model: White-box; attacker requires full access to model architecture, parameters, and gradients.
target_vulnerability: Exploits the model's sensitivity to small, carefully crafted input changes and the linearity of high-dimensional decision boundaries.

description: The ZOO (Zeroth Order Optimization) attack generates adversarial examples by estimating gradients using only model output probabilities, without requiring access to model internals.
mechanism: 1. The attacker queries the target CNN with perturbed inputs and observes output probabilities. 2. Finite differences are used to estimate the gradient of the loss with respect to the input. 3. The attacker iteratively updates the input in the direction that increases the loss (for untargeted) or decreases it towards a target class (for targeted). 4. This process continues until a successful adversarial example is found.
defence_mechanism: M-ZOO introduces stochastic elements and randomization in the model or input processing, making gradient estimation via finite differences unreliable. Sharpened edges or input transformations further distort the input-output mapping, reducing the attack's effectiveness by obfuscating the true gradient landscape.
variants: NES attack, Bandit attack, SPSA attack, Boundary attack
threat_model: black-box; attacker only needs access to model output probabilities (soft labels), not model parameters or gradients
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of the model to small, adversarially chosen input perturbations and the ability to estimate gradients from output probabilities

description: The Query Mechanism attack reduces the number of queries needed to craft adversarial examples against CNNs by optimizing the information gained from each query.
mechanism: 1. The attacker sends carefully chosen queries to the CNN, observing the model's outputs. 2. Using query reduction techniques, the attacker minimizes the number of queries by selecting inputs that maximize information gain. 3. The attacker iteratively refines perturbations based on feedback, converging on an adversarial example with fewer queries.
defence_mechanism: A-QM/Stochastic Element introduces randomness into the model's responses, making it harder for attackers to infer gradients or model behavior from queries; Sharpened Edges increase the model's sensitivity to small input changes, reducing the effectiveness of small perturbations.
variants: Adaptive Query Reduction, Bandit-based Query Attacks, NES-based Black-box Attacks
threat_model: black-box; attacker can query the model and observe outputs but has no access to internal parameters or gradients
target_vulnerability: The attack exploits the model's predictable output responses to input queries, enabling efficient search for adversarial perturbations.

description: Universal Adversarial Perturbations (UAP) are input-agnostic noise patterns that, when added to many images, cause a CNN to misclassify them while remaining mostly imperceptible to humans.
mechanism: 1. Collect a dataset of clean images. 2. Iteratively compute a single perturbation vector that, when added to each image, pushes it across the model's decision boundary. 3. Aggregate the minimal perturbations across the dataset to form a universal perturbation. 4. Apply this universal perturbation to new images to induce misclassification.
defence_mechanism: A-UAP introduces adversarial training with universal perturbations to increase robustness; stochastic elements randomize model responses, reducing the effectiveness of fixed perturbations; sharpening edges in preprocessing can suppress subtle, distributed noise patterns typical of UAPs.
variants: Class-wise UAP, Data-free UAP, Targeted UAP, GAN-based UAP
threat_model: White-box or grey-box; attacker requires access to model gradients or outputs to optimize the universal perturbation.
target_vulnerability: Exploits the model's high-dimensional linearity and shared decision boundaries, making it sensitive to small, structured perturbations across many inputs.

description: AutoZoom is a black-box adversarial attack that efficiently estimates gradients using random vector-based queries and autoencoder-based dimensionality reduction to craft optimal perturbations against CNNs.
mechanism: 1. The attacker trains an autoencoder to map input images to a lower-dimensional latent space. 2. Random vectors are sampled in this latent space to estimate the gradient of the loss with respect to the input. 3. The estimated gradient is used to iteratively update the input, generating adversarial examples with minimal queries. 4. The process continues until the adversarial example causes misclassification or meets a perturbation constraint.
defence_mechanism: A-AutoZoom introduces stochastic elements and sharpens edges in the input, making gradient estimation less reliable and reducing the effectiveness of random vector-based attacks by increasing input randomness and non-smoothness.
variants: ZOO, NES, Bandits Attack, AutoZOOM-B (bilinear), None well-known
threat_model: black-box; attacker can query the model and observe outputs (labels or probabilities) but has no access to model parameters or gradients
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to adversarial perturbations and the ability to estimate gradients via queries in a reduced latent space

description: GenAttack is a black-box adversarial attack that uses genetic algorithms to evolve input perturbations, aiming to mislead CNN classifiers while keeping changes imperceptible.
mechanism: 1. Initialize a population of perturbed images by adding random noise within (-δmax, δmax) to the original input. 2. Evaluate each candidate by querying the target model and measuring the adversarial objective (e.g., misclassification confidence). 3. Select the best-performing candidates and apply genetic operations (mutation, crossover) to generate a new population. 4. Repeat the process until an adversarial example is found or a maximum number of iterations is reached.
defence_mechanism: A-GenAttack introduces stochastic elements and sharpens edges in the input, making it harder for the genetic algorithm to find stable, transferable perturbations, and reducing the effectiveness of random noise-based search.
variants: None well-known
threat_model: black-box; attacker only needs query access to the model's outputs (predicted labels or confidence scores), without knowledge of model parameters or architecture.
target_vulnerability: Exploits the model's sensitivity to small, carefully crafted input perturbations and the lack of robustness to adversarially generated noise.

description: The Embedding COsine attack perturbs input data by adding random noise within a bounded range to maximize the cosine similarity between the perturbed input's embedding and a target direction, aiming to fool CNN classifiers.
mechanism: 1. For a given input, compute its embedding from an intermediate CNN layer. 2. Generate random noise within (-δmax, δmax) and add it to the input. 3. Evaluate the cosine similarity between the perturbed embedding and a target vector (e.g., another class or direction). 4. Select perturbations that maximize this similarity while remaining imperceptible.
defence_mechanism: A-ECO/Stochastic Element introduces randomness into the model's processing, making it harder for the attacker to optimize perturbations, while Sharpened Edges regularizes feature extraction to reduce sensitivity to small input changes, both mitigating the effectiveness of embedding-based attacks.
variants: Feature-space attacks, Embedding poisoning, None well-known
threat_model: white-box or grey-box; attacker needs access to model embeddings or intermediate layer outputs and the ability to query or compute gradients
target_vulnerability: Exploits the model's sensitivity to small changes in embedding space, particularly the alignment of feature vectors in CNNs

description: AAtack generates visible adversarial perturbations by adaptively initializing perturbations in directions that maximize model misclassification, targeting CNNs.
mechanism: 1. Compute the gradient of the loss with respect to the input image to identify sensitive directions. 2. Initialize perturbations adaptively along these directions, rather than randomly or uniformly. 3. Iteratively update the perturbation to maximize the model's prediction error while keeping the perturbation visible. 4. Apply the final perturbation to the input to induce misclassification.
defence_mechanism: A-AAttack/Stochastic Element introduces randomness into model predictions, making gradient-based attacks less effective, while Sharpened Edges preprocesses inputs to reduce the impact of visible perturbations by enhancing edge features and suppressing adversarial noise.
variants: Adaptive FGSM, Momentum Iterative Method, Projected Gradient Descent (PGD), None well-known
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to model architecture and gradients
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to input perturbations aligned with gradient directions, and over-reliance on specific input features

description: BayesOpt attacks use Bayesian Optimization to efficiently search for adversarial perturbations that fool CNNs, often by reducing the search space dimensionality for faster convergence.
mechanism: 1. Define an objective function measuring model misclassification under input perturbations. 2. Use Bayesian Optimization to propose perturbations, leveraging a surrogate model to predict promising candidates. 3. Apply dimensionality reduction (e.g., PCA, random projections) to limit the search space. 4. Iteratively update the surrogate and select new perturbations until a successful adversarial example is found.
defence_mechanism: A-BayesOpt/Stochastic Element introduces randomness into model predictions or optimization steps, making the attack's surrogate modeling less effective; Sharpened Edges refers to input preprocessing that removes subtle perturbations, reducing attack success.
variants: Black-box Bayesian attacks, NES-based black-box attacks, None well-known
threat_model: Black-box or grey-box; attacker needs query access to the model and knowledge of input/output pairs, but not model internals.
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to adversarial perturbations and the smoothness of the input-output mapping exploited by efficient search.

perturbation_search: Latent Space NES search and Gradient Based
description: The NES (Natural Evolution Strategies) attack generates adversarial examples by searching for effective perturbations in the latent space using evolutionary optimization and gradient information.
mechanism: 1. Encode the input into a latent representation using a suitable encoder. 2. Apply NES-based optimization in the latent space to search for perturbations that maximize the model's loss or misclassification probability. 3. Optionally use gradient information to guide the search more efficiently. 4. Decode the perturbed latent vector back to input space to obtain the adversarial example.
defence_mechanism: A-NES/Augmented Adversarial Training incorporates adversarial examples generated via NES into the training process, improving model robustness by exposing it to such attacks and reducing its susceptibility to latent space perturbations.
variants: Latent Space Attacks, Evolutionary Attack, Black-box NES Attack
threat_model: grey-box; attacker requires access to the model's outputs and, optionally, gradients or a surrogate encoder/decoder
target_vulnerability: Exploits the model's sensitivity to structured perturbations in the latent space, which can induce misclassification with minimal perceptual change.

perturbation_search: Latent Space NES search and Gradient Based
description: Transfer-NES-PGD generates adversarial examples by combining Natural Evolution Strategies (NES) search in the latent space with gradient-based PGD to craft perturbations that transfer across CNN models.
mechanism: 1. Map input data to a latent space representation. 2. Use NES to search for perturbations in the latent space that maximize model loss. 3. Project optimized latent perturbations back to input space. 4. Refine adversarial examples with PGD in input space for maximal effect.
defence_mechanism: A-T-NES-PGD/Augmented Adv Training defends by incorporating adversarial examples generated via NES-PGD into the training process, improving model robustness against both latent space and gradient-based attacks.
variants: NES-PGD, Transfer-PGD, Black-box NES attacks
threat_model: black-box or grey-box; attacker needs query access to the model and possibly access to a surrogate model for transferability
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to transferable adversarial perturbations and their reliance on local gradients

perturbation_search: Latent Space NES search and Gradient Based
description: Transfer-NES-FGSM generates adversarial examples by combining gradient-based perturbations with Natural Evolution Strategies (NES) search in the latent space, enabling attacks to transfer across different CNN models.
mechanism: 1. The attacker encodes the input into a latent space representation. 2. NES is used to search for perturbations in the latent space that maximize the model's loss. 3. The found perturbation is mapped back to input space. 4. FGSM (Fast Gradient Sign Method) is applied to further refine the adversarial example.
defence_mechanism: A-T-NES-FGSM/Augmented Adv Training defends by incorporating adversarial examples generated via NES-FGSM into the training process, improving model robustness against both gradient-based and latent space attacks.
variants: NES-FGSM, Transfer-FGSM, NES-based black-box attacks
threat_model: grey-box or black-box; attacker needs access to model outputs (predictions or confidence scores), but not model internals or gradients
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to transferable adversarial perturbations and their inability to generalize robustness to attacks crafted in latent space

description: P-RGF (Prior-guided Random Gradient-Free) is a black-box adversarial attack that estimates gradients using random search, guided by prior information, to craft optimal perturbations against CNNs.
mechanism: 1. The attacker queries the target CNN with perturbed inputs to estimate the gradient direction using random search. 2. Prior information (such as image structure or previous queries) is incorporated to guide the search and improve efficiency. 3. The estimated gradient is used to iteratively update the input, generating adversarial examples with minimal queries. 4. The process continues until a successful adversarial example is found or a query budget is exhausted.
defence_mechanism: A-P-RGF/AT (Adversarially-trained Prior-guided RGF) enhances model robustness by incorporating adversarial examples generated by P-RGF during training, making the model less sensitive to such gradient-free attacks.
variants: RGF, NES, Bandits, SimBA
threat_model: black-box; attacker can query the model and observe outputs (labels or probabilities), but has no access to model parameters or gradients
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to adversarial perturbations even when gradients are not directly accessible

description: Trans-P-RGF is a black-box adversarial attack that generates optimal perturbations by leveraging transferability and random gradient-free search to fool CNN models.
mechanism: 1. The attacker uses a surrogate model to craft adversarial examples, exploiting transferability to the target CNN. 2. Random gradient-free (RGF) optimization is applied to search for perturbations that maximize the loss on the surrogate. 3. The crafted perturbations are transferred and tested on the target model. 4. The process iterates to refine perturbations for optimal attack success.
defence_mechanism: A-Trans-P-RGF/AT employs adversarial training using adversarial examples generated by Trans-P-RGF, enhancing model robustness by exposing it to such perturbations during training.
variants: P-RGF, RGF, NES, Transfer-based attacks
threat_model: black-box; attacker has no access to model parameters or gradients but can query the model and may use surrogate models
target_vulnerability: Exploits the transferability of adversarial examples and the model's sensitivity to input perturbations

description: TREMBA is a black-box adversarial attack that generates visible perturbations by optimizing a latent code through random search to fool CNN models.
mechanism: 1. A generative model is trained to map latent codes to image perturbations. 2. For a given input, random latent codes are sampled and decoded into perturbations. 3. These perturbations are added to the input and queried against the target CNN. 4. The latent code is iteratively updated via random search to maximize the attack objective (e.g., misclassification).
defence_mechanism: A-TREMBA and adversarial training (AT) improve model robustness by incorporating adversarial examples, including those generated by TREMBA, into the training process, making the model less sensitive to such perturbations.
variants: A-TREMBA, AutoZOOM, NES, Boundary Attack
threat_model: black-box; attacker can query the model and observe outputs but has no access to model parameters or gradients
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to adversarial perturbations in the input space, even when the perturbations are visible and generated without gradient information

description: NTM-NPTM attacks generate adversarial examples by optimizing perturbations under various norms or transformations to fool CNNs in a visible manner.
mechanism: 1. The attacker selects a perturbation constraint (e.g., L∞, L2, JPEG-L∞, StAdv, ReColorAdv). 2. An optimization process crafts perturbations to maximize model misclassification while keeping changes visible but plausible. 3. The perturbed input is applied to the CNN, causing incorrect predictions. 4. The process may leverage knowledge of the model's gradients (white-box setting).
defence_mechanism: M-NTM and PAT (Projected Adversarial Training) defend by augmenting training data with adversarial examples generated using similar perturbation methods, improving model robustness to such attacks.
variants: StAdv, ReColorAdv, JPEG-L∞, None well-known
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to model parameters and gradients
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to small, structured, or perceptible input perturbations that exploit overfitting and lack of robustness to distributional shifts.

description: Watermarking attacks embed visible patterns or signals into training data using gradient-based methods, causing the CNN to learn and recognize these patterns as triggers.
mechanism: 1. The attacker selects a visible watermark pattern and superimposes it onto a subset of training images. 2. Using gradient-based optimization, the attacker adjusts the watermark or its placement to maximize its influence on the model's predictions. 3. The poisoned data is injected into the training set, causing the CNN to associate the watermark with specific outputs. 4. At inference, the presence of the watermark can trigger targeted or misclassified predictions.
defence_mechanism: A-Watermarking detects and removes suspicious or anomalous watermarks from data, while data sanitizing filters or cleanses training samples to eliminate embedded patterns before model training.
variants: Backdoor attacks, Trigger-based poisoning, Invisible watermarking
threat_model: white-box or grey-box; attacker needs access to the training data and knowledge of the model architecture or gradients
target_vulnerability: The model's tendency to overfit to spurious correlations or patterns present in the training data

description: This attack generates adversarial examples by iteratively applying gradient-based perturbations to training data, augmenting the dataset to poison the model during training.
mechanism: 1. Compute the gradient of the loss with respect to input images using the current CNN model. 2. Apply small, iterative perturbations to the images in the direction that maximizes the loss (non-fast, i.e., multi-step). 3. Add these adversarially perturbed images to the training set as augmented data. 4. Retrain or fine-tune the model on this poisoned dataset.
defence_mechanism: M-PGD-NonFast uses robust adversarial training with multi-step PGD to make the model resilient to similar gradient-based attacks, while Pixel Defend preprocesses inputs to remove adversarial perturbations before classification.
variants: PGD-based Data Poisoning, Adversarial Training with Data Augmentation, None well-known
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires access to model gradients and training data

description: TransferBased-NES attacks generate adversarial examples for a target CNN by estimating gradients using Natural Evolution Strategies (NES) on a surrogate model, enabling black-box attacks via transferability.
mechanism: 1. Train or select a surrogate CNN model similar to the target. 2. Use NES to estimate the gradient of the loss with respect to the input on the surrogate. 3. Craft adversarial perturbations using these estimated gradients. 4. Apply the perturbations to the target model, leveraging transferability for misclassification.
defence_mechanism: A-TB-NES and randomization defenses disrupt the transferability of adversarial examples by introducing randomness or adversarial training, making it harder for surrogate-based perturbations to succeed on the target model.
variants: NES-based black-box attacks, Transfer-based attacks, ZOO (Zeroth Order Optimization)
threat_model: black-box; attacker has no access to target model parameters or gradients but can query the model and may have access to a similar surrogate model
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to transferable adversarial perturbations and the similarity of decision boundaries between surrogate and target models

description: This attack adds optimally chosen Gaussian noise to input images to mislead a CNN into making incorrect predictions while keeping the perturbation minimally visible.
mechanism: 1. Compute the gradient of the loss with respect to the input image. 2. Use the gradient to determine the direction in which to add Gaussian noise for maximal impact. 3. Generate and add Gaussian noise constrained by a visibility threshold. 4. Feed the perturbed image to the CNN to induce misclassification.
defence_mechanism: PC=Gaussian Noise refers to preprocessing or augmenting inputs with random Gaussian noise, which can desensitize the model to similar noise-based perturbations and improve robustness.
variants: Random Gaussian Noise, Adversarial Gaussian Noise, FGSM, PGD

target_vulnerability: The attack exploits the model's sensitivity to small, structured input perturbations that are not perceptible to humans.

description: Projected Gradient Descent (PGD) is an iterative adversarial attack that perturbs input images to maximize model loss while keeping changes within a specified norm constraint.
mechanism: 1. Compute the gradient of the loss with respect to the input image. 2. Update the input by taking a small step in the direction of the gradient (sign or raw). 3. Project the perturbed input back onto the allowed perturbation set (e.g., within an L-infinity ball). 4. Repeat steps 1-3 for a fixed number of iterations.
defence_mechanism: M-M-PGD and BAT (Bilateral Adversarial Training) defend by incorporating adversarial examples generated via multi-step PGD into the training process, making the model robust to similar iterative attacks.
variants: FGSM, BIM, CW, Auto-PGD
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to model parameters and gradients
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to small, norm-bounded input perturbations that exploit local linearity and overfitting to training data

description: Gradient Descent attacks craft adversarial examples by iteratively adjusting input data in the direction that maximally increases model loss, causing misclassification with minimal perturbation.
mechanism: 1. Compute the gradient of the loss with respect to the input image using the CNN's parameters. 2. Modify the input by a small step in the direction of the gradient (or its sign) to increase the loss. 3. Repeat the process until the perturbation reaches a predefined threshold or the model misclassifies the input. 4. Output the perturbed input as the adversarial example.
defence_mechanism: M-Gradient Descent and Adversarial Retraining defend by incorporating adversarial examples into the training process, making the model more robust to gradient-based perturbations by minimizing loss on both clean and adversarially perturbed data.
variants: FGSM, BIM, PGD, DeepFool, Carlini-Wagner
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to model architecture and gradients
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to small, input-space perturbations due to high-dimensional, non-linear decision boundaries

description: JPEG-Lp attacks craft adversarial examples by combining additive pixel perturbations with manipulations in the JPEG compression domain, producing visible but effective changes that fool CNNs.
mechanism: 1. The attacker generates an initial adversarial perturbation using an Lp-norm constraint. 2. This perturbation is then assembled or embedded into the image's JPEG compressed representation, possibly by modifying DCT coefficients. 3. The perturbed image is reconstructed and fed to the CNN, causing misclassification.
defence_mechanism: M-JPEG-Lp and JPEG Compression defenses work by re-encoding incoming images using JPEG compression, which tends to remove or attenuate adversarial perturbations embedded in the JPEG domain or as high-frequency noise, thus restoring model robustness.
variants: JPEG-Compressed Adversarial Examples, DCT-based Attacks, None well-known
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires access to the model parameters and gradients to optimize perturbations in both pixel and JPEG domains
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to small, structured perturbations in both pixel and frequency (JPEG) domains, and their inability to distinguish adversarial artifacts from legitimate image content

description: APGD-AT-Randomization is an adversarial attack that combines Auto-PGD (APGD) with randomization techniques to generate optimal perturbations against CNNs, often bypassing defenses that rely on deterministic gradients.
mechanism: 1. Initialize a random perturbation within the allowed norm ball. 2. Iteratively apply APGD steps, each time introducing randomization (e.g., input or gradient noise) to avoid local minima and gradient masking. 3. Aggregate or select the perturbation that maximizes the model's loss. 4. Output the adversarial example with optimal perturbation.
defence_mechanism: M-APGD-AT/Randomization counters this attack by training the model with adversarial examples generated using multiple APGD runs and randomization, making the model robust to both deterministic and randomized attacks.
variants: APGD, APGD-AT, Randomized PGD, Ensemble Adversarial Training
threat_model: white-box; attacker has full access to model parameters and gradients, including knowledge of any randomization layers
target_vulnerability: Exploits gradient masking and non-deterministic defenses by leveraging random search to find effective adversarial perturbations

description: APGD-AT-Logit Squeezing is an adversarial attack that generates optimal perturbations using Auto-PGD while leveraging logit squeezing to reduce model confidence and increase susceptibility to adversarial examples.
mechanism: 1. The attacker applies Auto-PGD (APGD), an iterative projected gradient descent method, to craft adversarial examples targeting the model. 2. During optimization, logit squeezing is used to minimize the difference between the highest and second-highest logits, making the model less confident and more vulnerable. 3. Random search is used to initialize or enhance the perturbation search space. 4. The process iterates until an optimal adversarial perturbation is found within the allowed norm.
defence_mechanism: M-APGD-AT (multi-step adversarial training with APGD) trains the model on strong APGD-generated adversarial examples, while logit squeezing regularizes the logits to prevent overconfidence, making it harder for the attack to find effective perturbations.
variants: APGD, PGD-AT, Logit Squeezing Attack, None well-known
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to model parameters and gradients
target_vulnerability: Exploits the model's overconfident predictions and sensitivity to small input perturbations

description: Momentum-Mustafa is an adversarial attack that generates optimal perturbations for CNNs by leveraging momentum-based iterative optimization to craft more transferable and effective adversarial examples.
mechanism: 1. Compute the gradient of the loss with respect to the input image. 2. Accumulate a velocity vector using momentum from previous gradients to stabilize and accelerate the perturbation search. 3. Update the input image iteratively by applying the momentum-augmented perturbation. 4. Repeat until the perturbation reaches the optimal threshold or misclassification is achieved.
defence_mechanism: M-Momentum/ Mustafa defence introduces momentum-based adversarial training or input preprocessing that anticipates and neutralizes momentum-driven perturbations by simulating such attacks during training or filtering them at inference.
variants: Momentum Iterative Method (MIM), Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM), Projected Gradient Descent (PGD)
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to model architecture and gradients
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to small, structured input perturbations that exploit gradient information for misclassification

description: The Momentum Iterative-Super resolution attack generates adversarial examples by iteratively applying perturbations with momentum, targeting CNNs, and then upscaling the perturbed images using super-resolution techniques to maintain perceptual quality.
mechanism: 1. Compute adversarial perturbations using the momentum iterative method, which accumulates gradients to stabilize and enhance attack effectiveness. 2. Apply these perturbations to the input image over multiple iterations. 3. Upscale the adversarial image using a super-resolution model to restore or enhance visual quality. 4. Feed the super-resolved adversarial image to the target CNN for misclassification.
defence_mechanism: M-Momentum Iterative defense uses adversarial training with momentum-based attacks to improve robustness, while Super Resolution defense applies upscaling to input images, which can remove or diminish adversarial perturbations by altering high-frequency artifacts.
variants: Momentum Iterative Method (MIM), Projected Gradient Descent (PGD), Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM), Super-Resolution Adversarial Attack (SRAA)
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to the model architecture and gradients
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to small, structured perturbations and their inability to distinguish between genuine and adversarial high-frequency details, especially after super-resolution processing

description: Momentum-Denoising attacks craft adversarial examples for CNNs by iteratively applying perturbations guided by momentum, while simultaneously reducing the impact of denoising defences.
mechanism: 1. Compute the gradient of the loss with respect to the input image. 2. Accumulate gradients across iterations using a momentum term to stabilize and amplify effective directions. 3. Apply iterative perturbations to the input, constrained by a norm bound. 4. Optionally, adapt perturbations to counteract image denoising defences.
defence_mechanism: M-Momentum/ Image Denoising defences apply denoising filters (e.g., non-local means, total variation minimization) to remove adversarial noise, and use momentum-based adversarial training to increase robustness against momentum-driven attacks.
variants: Momentum Iterative Method (MIM), Projected Gradient Descent (PGD), Basic Iterative Method (BIM)
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to model architecture and gradients
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to small, structured perturbations that exploit gradient information and are not fully removed by standard denoising techniques

description: This attack crafts adversarial examples by optimizing perturbations that remain effective even after input discretization, such as quantization or one-hot encoding, to fool CNNs.
mechanism: 1. Compute gradients of the loss with respect to the input image. 2. Optimize perturbations that, after discretization (e.g., rounding or one-hot mapping), still cause misclassification. 3. Apply the perturbation to the input and discretize the result. 4. Feed the discretized, perturbed input to the CNN to induce an incorrect prediction.
defence_mechanism: M-Discretized Inputs/OneHot defences map inputs to a discrete set (e.g., quantized pixel values or one-hot vectors), reducing the effect of small, adversarial perturbations by nullifying changes that do not cross discretization thresholds.
variants: Expectation Over Transformation (EOT) for discretization, Quantization-aware attacks
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to model parameters and gradients, including knowledge of the discretization process
target_vulnerability: Sensitivity of CNNs to small input changes and their inability to handle non-differentiable or quantized input spaces robustly

description: Gradient-based adversarial attacks generate small, carefully crafted perturbations to input images by leveraging the gradients of a CNN's loss function, causing the model to misclassify the perturbed inputs.
mechanism: 1. Compute the gradient of the loss with respect to the input image using backpropagation. 2. Construct an adversarial perturbation by optimizing the input in the direction that maximizes the loss (e.g., using L∞, L2, or L1 norms). 3. Add the perturbation to the original input to create an adversarial example. 4. Feed the adversarial example to the model to induce misclassification.
defence_mechanism: M-Gradient Based and BAT (Byzantine Adversarial Training) defenses mitigate gradient-based attacks by incorporating adversarial examples during training, making the model robust to such perturbations and reducing the effectiveness of gradient-based optimization.
variants: FGSM, BIM, PGD (PGDL∞, PGDL2, PGDL1), DeepFool, Carlini-Wagner
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to the model architecture and gradients
target_vulnerability: The attack exploits the model's sensitivity to small, input-aligned perturbations due to high-dimensional, non-linear decision boundaries.

description: PGD Fast is an accelerated version of Projected Gradient Descent that generates adversarial examples by quickly finding optimal perturbations within a specified norm bound to fool CNNs.
mechanism: 1. Compute the gradient of the loss with respect to the input image. 2. Apply a fast, possibly single-step or few-step, update in the direction of the gradient to maximize the loss, constrained by a norm (e.g., L-infinity). 3. Project the perturbed image back into the allowed perturbation set if necessary. 4. Repeat for a small number of iterations or use a larger step size for speed.
defence_mechanism: M-PGD Fast uses multiple random starts and fast PGD steps during adversarial training to increase robustness, while data augmentation exposes the model to diverse inputs, reducing sensitivity to small perturbations.
variants: FGSM, Basic Iterative Method (BIM), Standard PGD, Momentum Iterative Method (MIM)
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to model parameters and gradients
target_vulnerability: Exploits the model's linearity and sensitivity to small, adversarially chosen input perturbations

description: The M-Gradient Based attack generates adversarial examples for CNNs by iteratively applying optimal perturbations, using momentum to accelerate and stabilize the search for effective input modifications.
mechanism: 1. Compute the gradient of the loss with respect to the input image. 2. Accumulate a velocity vector using momentum from previous gradients. 3. Update the input by applying a scaled sign of the accumulated gradient, constrained by a perturbation budget. 4. Repeat for several iterations to maximize misclassification.
defence_mechanism: M-MGA/Vector Defence mitigates this attack by projecting inputs onto a manifold of legitimate data or by filtering out adversarial directions in the input space, thereby neutralizing perturbations aligned with the attack's momentum-driven updates.
variants: Momentum Iterative Method (MIM), Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM), Basic Iterative Method (BIM), Projected Gradient Descent (PGD)
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to model architecture, parameters, and gradients
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to small, adversarially crafted perturbations due to high-dimensional, non-linear decision boundaries

description: IGB-Adam is a gradient-based adversarial attack that generates optimal perturbations by leveraging the Adam optimizer to efficiently maximize model loss on CNNs.
mechanism: 1. Compute the gradient of the loss with respect to the input image using the target CNN. 2. Use the Adam optimizer to iteratively update the input, searching for a perturbation that maximizes the loss while staying within a norm constraint. 3. Apply the optimal perturbation to the input to create an adversarial example.
defence_mechanism: A-IGB-Adam/Vector Defence mitigates the attack by adversarial training with IGB-Adam-generated examples and/or projecting inputs onto a lower-dimensional vector space to reduce the effect of adversarial perturbations.
variants: IGB-SGD, PGD, FGSM
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to model architecture, parameters, and gradients
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to small, input-constrained perturbations that exploit the model's local linearity and gradient information

description: The image scaling attack manipulates input images so that, after resizing (scaling) by the model's preprocessing pipeline, the resulting image is adversarial or misleading, even though the original appears benign.
mechanism: 1. Attacker crafts an image that looks normal at its original resolution. 2. The image is uploaded or input to the system, which automatically resizes it (e.g., downscaling to a fixed size). 3. The scaling process causes the image to morph into a different, adversarial pattern that fools the CNN. 4. The model processes the scaled image, leading to misclassification.
defence_mechanism: A-Image Scaling/RobustScaling applies preprocessing techniques that make the scaling operation less sensitive to adversarial manipulations, such as using anti-aliasing, randomized resizing, or robust interpolation methods to preserve semantic content.
variants: Downscaling Attack, Upscaling Attack, None well-known
threat_model: black-box; attacker needs knowledge of the input preprocessing pipeline and the scaling algorithm but not model internals
target_vulnerability: Exploits the model's reliance on scaled inputs and the non-robustness of standard image scaling algorithms to crafted perturbations

description: M-PGD (Momentum Projected Gradient Descent) is an adversarial attack that iteratively perturbs input images using momentum-augmented gradients to find minimal, optimal perturbations that fool CNNs.
mechanism: 1. Compute the gradient of the loss with respect to the input image. 2. Accumulate gradients using a momentum term to stabilize and accelerate updates. 3. Update the input by taking a step in the direction of the accumulated gradient, projecting back into the allowed perturbation set if necessary. 4. Repeat for a fixed number of iterations or until misclassification.
defence_mechanism: Gradient Based/Vector Defence methods counter M-PGD by either masking or regularizing gradients (e.g., gradient obfuscation, adversarial training) or by projecting inputs onto a lower-dimensional or robust vector space, making it harder for gradient-based attacks to find effective perturbations.
variants: PGD, FGSM, MI-FGSM, BIM
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to model architecture and gradients
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to small, adversarially crafted perturbations due to high-dimensional, non-linear decision boundaries

description: DeepFool is an iterative adversarial attack that minimally perturbs an input image to push it across the nearest decision boundary of a classifier, causing misclassification.
mechanism: 1. Compute the gradient of the classifier's output with respect to the input image. 2. Approximate the classifier locally as linear and estimate the closest decision boundary. 3. Iteratively apply the smallest perturbation required to cross this boundary. 4. Repeat until the classifier's prediction changes.
defence_mechanism: A-DeepFool generates adversarial examples using DeepFool and incorporates them into adversarial retraining, making the model more robust by exposing it to such perturbations during training.
variants: A-DeepFool, L2-DeepFool, DeepFool for multiclass, None well-known
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to model architecture and gradients
target_vulnerability: Exploits the model's linearity and sensitivity near decision boundaries in high-dimensional input space

description: Cassidi is a visible adversarial attack on CNNs that perturbs input images using the gradient sign method to create misclassifications while keeping changes perceptible.
mechanism: 1. Compute the gradient of the loss with respect to the input image. 2. Apply the sign of the gradient to the input, scaled by a chosen step size, to generate a visibly perturbed image. 3. Feed the perturbed image to the CNN to induce misclassification.
defence_mechanism: A-Cassidi and adversarial retraining defend by augmenting the training data with Cassidi-generated adversarial examples, enabling the model to learn robust features and correctly classify perturbed inputs.
variants: FGSM, BIM, PGD
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires access to model parameters and gradients
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to gradient-based input perturbations due to linearity and high-dimensional input space

description: NewtonFool is an adversarial attack that iteratively perturbs an input to reduce the model's confidence in its predicted class, eventually causing misclassification.
mechanism: 1. Compute the gradient of the model's output with respect to the input for the predicted class. 2. Use a Newton-like iterative method to find the minimal perturbation that reduces the model's confidence below a threshold. 3. Update the input in the direction that most efficiently decreases the predicted class score. 4. Repeat until the model misclassifies the input or a maximum number of iterations is reached.
defence_mechanism: A-NewtonFool adapts the attack's mechanism to improve robustness, while adversarial retraining augments the training data with NewtonFool-generated adversarial examples, making the model more resilient to such perturbations.
variants: A-NewtonFool, None well-known
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to model architecture and gradients
target_vulnerability: Exploits the model's sensitivity to small, targeted input perturbations that can significantly reduce output confidence.

description: TUAP (Targeted Universal Adversarial Perturbation) generates a single, visible perturbation that, when added to any input, causes a CNN to misclassify it into a specific target class.
mechanism: 1. Collect a representative dataset of inputs for the target CNN. 2. Iteratively optimize a universal perturbation by maximizing the model's prediction confidence for a chosen target class across the dataset. 3. Constrain the perturbation to be visible but within a specified norm bound. 4. Apply the resulting perturbation to new inputs to induce targeted misclassification.
defence_mechanism: A-TUAP and adversarial retraining involve augmenting the training data with adversarially perturbed examples (including TUAPs), enabling the model to learn to correctly classify perturbed inputs and thus increasing robustness against such attacks.
variants: Universal Adversarial Perturbation (UAP), Class-wise UAP, None well-known
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to the model architecture and parameters to compute effective universal perturbations
target_vulnerability: The attack exploits the model's linearity and shared feature representations, making it susceptible to input-agnostic perturbations that generalize across many samples.

description: DFO (Derivative-Free Optimization) attacks generate adversarial examples for CNNs without requiring gradient information by optimizing input perturbations using black-box queries.
mechanism: 1. The attacker queries the CNN model with perturbed inputs and observes the output probabilities or labels. 2. Using a derivative-free optimization algorithm (e.g., evolutionary strategies, random search), the attacker iteratively updates the input to maximize the attack objective (e.g., misclassification). 3. The process repeats until a successful adversarial example is found within allowed perturbation bounds.
defence_mechanism: A-DFO/Adversarial Retraining augments the training data with adversarial examples generated by DFO attacks, enabling the CNN to learn robust features and reduce susceptibility to such perturbations.
variants: NES (Natural Evolution Strategies), SPSA (Simultaneous Perturbation Stochastic Approximation), Bandit attacks
threat_model: black-box; attacker can query the model and observe outputs but does not have access to model internals or gradients
target_vulnerability: The attack exploits the model's sensitivity to small input perturbations and the lack of robustness to non-gradient-based adversarial manipulations.

description: The Salt-Pepper attack introduces random pixels set to maximum (white) or minimum (black) values in an image, visibly corrupting it to degrade CNN performance.
mechanism: 1. Select a subset of image pixels at random. 2. Replace each selected pixel with either the minimum (0) or maximum (255) intensity value. 3. Repeat for a specified proportion of pixels to achieve the desired noise level. 4. Feed the perturbed image to the CNN for inference.
defence_mechanism: A-Salt-Pepper/Filter applies median or adaptive filters to the input image, removing isolated extreme-value pixels and restoring the image's original structure, thereby mitigating the attack's effect.
variants: Random-valued impulse noise, Gaussian noise, Speckle noise
threat_model: black-box; attacker only needs access to input data and does not require knowledge of model parameters or architecture
target_vulnerability: CNNs' sensitivity to local pixel-level perturbations and lack of robustness to non-smooth, high-magnitude noise

description: The cADV attack generates visible adversarial perturbations by leveraging hints and masks to selectively modify image regions, misleading CNN classifiers while maintaining human-recognizable content.
mechanism: 1. Identify salient or semantically important regions in the input image using a hint or mask. 2. Apply structured perturbations to these regions to maximize model misclassification while keeping changes visible but plausible. 3. Optimize perturbations iteratively, often using gradient-based methods, to ensure attack success. 4. Output the adversarial image with visible but targeted modifications.
defence_mechanism: A-cADV detects and reverses cADV perturbations by analyzing adversarial patterns, while JPEG Compression removes high-frequency artifacts introduced by the attack, reducing its effectiveness.
variants: AdvMask, AdvCam, Semantic Adversarial Examples
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires access to model gradients and architecture to craft targeted perturbations
target_vulnerability: CNNs' over-reliance on specific spatial features and sensitivity to structured, localized perturbations

description: AtADV is an adversarial attack that perturbs images in the color space to make them resemble a target class, causing CNNs to misclassify them while keeping changes visible but plausible.
mechanism: 1. Select a source image and a target class (Ts). 2. Search for minimal perturbations in the color space that move the image's representation closer to the target class centroid. 3. Apply these color modifications to the image, ensuring the changes are visible but not excessive. 4. Feed the perturbed image to the CNN, inducing misclassification as the target class.
defence_mechanism: JPEG compression removes high-frequency and subtle color perturbations by quantizing color information, thereby reducing or eliminating the adversarial color changes introduced by AtADV.
variants: ColorFool, AdvColor, None well-known
threat_model: white-box or grey-box; attacker needs access to the model or its gradients to optimize color perturbations
target_vulnerability: CNNs' sensitivity to color distribution and reliance on color features for classification

description: This attack uses a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) to create adversarial examples that visibly alter input images to fool a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) classifier.
mechanism: 1. Train a GAN to generate images or perturbations that, when added to legitimate inputs, cause misclassification by the target CNN. 2. Assemble or combine generated perturbations with original images to maximize the attack's effectiveness. 3. Evaluate and iteratively refine the GAN based on the CNN's feedback to improve adversarial success.
defence_mechanism: Adversarial training augments the training data with GAN-generated adversarial examples, enabling the CNN to learn robust features and correctly classify both clean and adversarially perturbed images.
variants: AdvGAN, Conditional GAN attacks, GAN-based data poisoning
threat_model: white-box or grey-box; attacker needs access to the model architecture and/or gradients, and a dataset to train the GAN
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to adversarially crafted inputs and their inability to generalize well to out-of-distribution or manipulated data

description: The Fast Minimum-norm (FMN) Attack efficiently finds the smallest possible perturbation that causes a CNN to misclassify an input, ensuring the adversarial example is as close as possible to the original image.
mechanism: 1. Initialize the perturbation with a small value. 2. Formulate the attack as a constrained optimization problem using a Lagrangian approach to balance misclassification and minimal perturbation. 3. Iteratively update the perturbation via gradient descent on the Lagrangian objective, adjusting the constraint multiplier to enforce minimal norm. 4. Stop when the adversarial example is misclassified with the smallest possible perturbation.
defence_mechanism: Adversarial Training exposes the model to adversarial examples, including minimal-norm perturbations, during training, improving robustness by teaching the model to correctly classify such perturbed inputs.
variants: Carlini & Wagner (C&W) Attack, Projected Gradient Descent (PGD), DeepFool
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires full access to model parameters and gradients
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of CNNs to small, carefully crafted input perturbations that exploit the model's decision boundary geometry

mechanism: 1. The attacker crafts adversarial perturbations in the input that subtly alter attention weights. 2. The manipulated attention pattern allows the input to bypass safety filters, leading to unauthorized or unsafe responses. 4. The attack iteratively refines perturbations based on model feedback to maximize jailbreak success.

variants: Prompt Injection, Attention Hijacking, Gradient-based Jailbreaks, None well-known
threat_model: grey-box; attacker needs query access to the model and some knowledge of its attention mechanisms or output behaviors

description: LinBP is a data poisoning attack targeting linear regression models by injecting carefully crafted malicious data points into the training set to bias the learned parameters.
mechanism: 1. The attacker selects a subset of training data to poison. 2. Random perturbations are applied to the features and/or labels of these points. 3. The poisoned data is injected into the training set. 4. The model is retrained, causing its parameters to shift towards the attacker's objective.
defence_mechanism: LinBP/Pixel Defend mitigates the attack by detecting and removing or correcting anomalous data points during training, often using robust statistics or input sanitization to reduce the influence of poisoned samples.
variants: Influence attack, Label flipping, Back-gradient poisoning
threat_model: white-box or grey-box; attacker needs access to the training data and knowledge of the model architecture
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of linear regression to outliers and the influence of individual data points on parameter estimation

description: This attack perturbs input data within a specified L∞ norm bound to fool hierarchical models, using random search to find effective adversarial examples. The perturbations are visible, meaning they can be detected by human observers.
mechanism: 1. The attacker selects an input sample and defines an L∞ norm bound for perturbations. 2. Random perturbations within this bound are applied to the input. 3. The perturbed input is fed into the hierarchical model. 4. The process repeats until a perturbation is found that causes misclassification or degrades model performance.
defence_mechanism: M-L∞-bounded and TRADES defenses train the model with adversarial examples constrained by the L∞ norm, improving robustness by minimizing the worst-case loss within the L∞ ball and balancing accuracy and robustness via regularization.
variants: FGSM, PGD, DeepFool, BIM
threat_model: white-box; attacker requires access to the model architecture and gradients to effectively craft perturbations
target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of hierarchical models to small, norm-bounded input perturbations that exploit local linearity and insufficient adversarial robustness.

description: SVR poisoning attacks inject carefully crafted data points into the training set to manipulate the predictions of Support Vector Regression (SVR) or Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) models. The attacker aims to degrade model accuracy or force specific outputs.
mechanism: 1. The attacker selects or generates poisoning points with feature and label values designed to maximize model error or bias predictions. 2. These points are inserted into the training data. 3. The SVR/GPR model is retrained on the poisoned dataset, causing the regression boundary or function to shift. 4. The attack is evaluated by measuring the impact on model predictions or error rates.
defence_mechanism: DBSCAN is used to cluster the training data and identify outliers, which are likely to be poisoning points; these outliers can then be removed before training SVR or GPR, reducing the attack's effectiveness.
variants: Label flipping, Gradient-based poisoning, Influence function attacks
threat_model: white-box or grey-box; attacker needs access to the training data and knowledge of the model type and hyperparameters
target_vulnerability: Sensitivity of SVR/GPR to outliers and anomalous data points in the training set

description: The Vanilla Universal-UAP attack generates a single, visible perturbation that, when added to any input, causes a black-box or unknown model to misclassify a wide range of samples.
mechanism: 1. Collect a representative set of input samples. 2. Iteratively apply random perturbations to these samples and evaluate the model's outputs (using queries or feedback). 3. Aggregate perturbations that consistently cause misclassification across many samples. 4. Output a universal perturbation that is effective on most inputs.
defence_mechanism: A-UAP/Adversarial Training augments the training data with adversarially perturbed samples, teaching the model to correctly classify inputs even when universal perturbations are present, thereby increasing robustness.
variants: Universal Adversarial Perturbations (UAP), Data-Dependent UAP, Class-Universal Perturbations

Generate random perturbations focused on these dominant features to maximize misclassification. 3. Aggregate perturbations across multiple samples to create a universal perturbation. 4. Apply the universal perturbation to new inputs to induce misclassification in the target model.

description: GAP-UAP is a black-box universal adversarial perturbation attack that generates perceptible noise to fool models without requiring access to model internals.
mechanism: 1. The attacker queries the target model with random inputs and observes outputs. 2. Random perturbations are iteratively added to inputs to find a universal noise pattern that causes misclassification across many samples. 3. The process continues until a perturbation is found that generalizes to most inputs. 4. The final universal perturbation is applied to new data to induce errors.
defence_mechanism: A-GAP-UAP and adversarial training defend by augmenting training data with adversarially perturbed examples, improving model robustness to universal and perceptual perturbations like those generated by GAP-UAP.

threat_model: black-box; attacker only needs query access to the model's outputs, not internal parameters or gradients

description: Cos-UAP is a black-box universal adversarial perturbation attack that generates a single perturbation vector capable of fooling a target model across many inputs by maximizing the cosine similarity between the perturbation and the model's loss gradients.
mechanism: 1. The attacker queries the target model with a set of clean inputs and collects the model's outputs. 2. For each input, the attacker estimates the gradient direction (using finite differences or surrogate models) and computes the cosine similarity between candidate perturbations and these gradients. 3. The perturbation is iteratively updated in the direction that maximizes the average cosine similarity across the dataset, subject to a norm constraint. 4. The final universal perturbation is applied to new inputs to induce misclassification.
defence_mechanism: A-Cos-UAP and adversarial training defend by incorporating adversarial examples generated via Cos-UAP into the training process, enabling the model to learn robust features and reduce its sensitivity to such universal perturbations.
variants: UAP, Fast Feature Fool, GAP, None well-known
threat_model: black-box; attacker only needs query access to the model's outputs for a set of inputs, without knowledge of model parameters or architecture
target_vulnerability: The attack exploits the model's shared decision boundary directions across many inputs, leveraging the alignment of loss gradients to craft a universal perturbation.

description: FFF is a black-box adversarial attack that generates perceptually similar adversarial examples by applying random perturbations to input data and observing model outputs.
mechanism: 1. The attacker queries the target model with randomly perturbed versions of an input. 2. The attacker observes the model's output labels or confidence scores. 3. Perturbations are iteratively refined based on observed outputs to find an input that causes misclassification while remaining perceptually similar to the original.

target_vulnerability: The model's sensitivity to small, random input perturbations that are imperceptible to humans but can cause misclassification

description: The AAA attack generates adversarial examples by applying random perceptual perturbations to input data, aiming to fool a black-box or unknown model without requiring internal knowledge.
mechanism: 1. The attacker queries the target model with original inputs and records outputs. 2. Random perturbations, constrained to be perceptually similar, are applied to the inputs. 3. The perturbed inputs are submitted to the model to observe if the output changes. 4. Successful perturbations that cause misclassification are selected as adversarial examples.

variants: None well-known

target_vulnerability: Susceptibility of the model to small, random, perceptually insignificant input changes that can alter predictions

description: Class Discriminative Universal Adversarial Perturbations (UAPs) are input-agnostic perturbations crafted to consistently mislead a model into predicting a specific target class, even when the model's internals are unknown.
mechanism: 1. The attacker queries the black-box model with a set of clean samples. 2. Random perturbations are iteratively added to these samples, aiming to maximize misclassification into a chosen target class. 3. The process continues until a universal perturbation is found that, when added to any input, causes the model to predict the target class with high probability. 4. The final perturbation is perceptually constrained to remain visually inconspicuous.
defence_mechanism: A-GD-UAP and adversarial training defend by augmenting training data with adversarially perturbed examples, enabling the model to learn robust features and reducing its susceptibility to universal or class-targeted perturbations.
